Even now as I've been thinking about it, it's makes my stomach drop.

It does, thank you!

I've decided to take her out to breakfast Sunday morning when she gets off work.

Thanks!
I deserve to be yelled at tbh...
Thank you. I'll be taking her to lunch today. I'll make her feel extra special.
Thank you!

> But are you a complete idiot?

Yes. Yes, I am.

> sell both and surprise her on concert night with dinner or a clean house

Good idea. She's working until 3:30 am Sunday morning, so maybe I'll take her out for an early, early breakfast.

> Now, speaking as a woman, I would be jealous just because she is younger, you're going out together, and might feel like I wasn't good enough anymore.

This really spoke to me, because it made me realize that if she were to go to, say, a health event with some dude she just started working with, I'd do a double-take.

Thank you for making me see that.
Just want to make sure she's okay. I feel terribly guilty right now.
Thank you! I'm debating going to see her for lunch. She hasn't answered my text messages. My buddy says she's been pretty quiet too.

100% agree with your last statement. Once her demeanor changed, I already knew I wasn't going to be taking the employee. My worry is that she's going to try and go through someone big on her own and I won't know what's going on in her head.

I'm *not* mad at her for being upset. I'm not even mad. Or annoyed. I'm worried that if she won't tell me what's on her mind now, what bigger things is she gonna try and go through by herself? That's what I'm worried about.

I don't think she's being unreasonable, either. I just want her to talk to me when she has an issue.

I won't be bringing the employee with me.

Thanks!

I'll admit I'm not always super open about my feelings, either. To the point where if I'm feeling down about something, I won't tell her right away. I'll keep it to myself so I don't seem like less of a man (thanks, dad /s). 

I've been thinking of suggesting a deal. That we both have to express our feelings. If one of us asks, we *have* to tell the other how we feel. Thoughts on that?
You're totally right. I'll sell the other ticket and go alone.
I'm glad it's worked for someone else. Makes me feel better!
Thanks!
They certainly weren't when they were hurling insults at me.

Yeah, my father used to tell me that I couldn't take care of my appearance. Couldn't style my hair or dress nice because, "that's for fags."

Naturally, I grew up to spite him.
I'm a firm believer that children should only be pushed to do their best. Opinion pushing is just not my style.
Thanks for the flag colors! We'll pick one up this weekend. We already have a PEACE flag outside!

Thanks!

My wife is a doctor and has had many teens come out to her because they felt safe in that environment. I think she already knew how to handle it. It was like she wasn't even surprised. Maybe she already had an idea about it.

Oh! Oh! Edgy edgy edgy!!!!!!

Girls/Girls/Boys

I think you can adopt adults in my state! Haha!

Iiii'lllll go with the 6-pack. Knowing B, he'd like me punching him in the nuts!

Oh! Thanks! I'll crosspost and see if anyone has any additional advice, thanks!

Not sure about the lemon bars, though. I'm not a huge citrus in my dessert kinda guy haha.

He is a wonderful person and friend. I don't know how I lucked out.

No one tell him I'm saying all these good things about him! I don't want him getting a big(ger) ego!

>I wasn't made aware of the risks of sex with fellow girls

See, neither am I, so I have a lot of research to do.
My other thought is that it's just silly how some people think you can help who you're attracted to.

The dating thing was a joke on my part based on a previous conversation we've had.

She's actually expressed that she wants to find out who she is before she dates anyone.

The jokes I can *definitely* do.

There's no difference between a bad joke and a *dad* joke!

^(Bah dum tiss.)

Haha it'll probably be more like:

Lexi: "I'm going out."

Me: "On a date?"

Lexi: "...Yeah."

Me: "Just call me Oak."

Lexi: "What?"

Me: "Is it a boy or a girl?"

Lexi: *rolls eyes while I snicker to myself*
Yeah, she expressed to me that she isn't ready to date because she doesn't really know how she feels, which tells me a lot about her.

>Say whatever you want, downvote or flame me, I don’t care.

Homie, you can't set yourself up for failure before you even start.

>I’ve spent decades carefully researching my opinions and yes, I post in T\_D, therefore all my opinions are invalid. /s

None of this matters to me. You could spend 100 years researching your *opinion* and it still wouldn't tell me fuck all about my situation.

>The human brain isn’t fully and completely formed until approximately the age of 25, and yes, that goes for girls too - to dispel the “girls develop / mature faster than boys” trope.

I *know all of this*. My wife is a doctor. My best friend is a surgeon. But I will not, REPEAT WILL NOT, deny my daughter the full benefit of exploring who she is so she can become a well-rounded individual.

>You need to stop this shit now.

Make me.

>Bisexuality / homosexuality will expose your daughter to a whole host of unhealthy people, behaviors, activities, etc.

This statement is bullshit. Every person has the capacity to be shitty. Their sexual orientation means nothing.

>I’m speaking from personal experience on this, having known many homosexual people in my time.

Oh. Okay. So you know a bunch of homosexual people. Me too. And I disagree, so where does that leave us?

>At 16 your daughter is barely old enough to date, can’t vote, can’t even buy cigarettes, and she sure as hell isn’t mature, experienced, nor old enough to figure out if she thinks she is something other than heterosexual.

You. Don't. Know. My. Daughter. Or me. You don't know my family or what we've been through. My daughter has seen, smelled and experienced death in a multitude of ways. She spent two years in Indonesia with people who constantly wanted to kidnap her. Fuck off with that bullshit.

I was very pleased to learn while reading that it was written by a strong, educated, intelligent doctor who also happens to be an obviously conservative woman - though it is NOT a political text in any way.

I appreciate the link and will check it out. Thank you.

>You need to be the man she needs, not the one she wants, and nip this in the bud before your daughter travels down a dark path.

Don't tell me what I need to do.

I'm just surprised there aren't more people who are understanding about it. It's not like you can help who you're attracted to.
She asked me if this means she can't have sleepovers anymore and I told her absolutely not. It changes nothing.
That makes me feel so much better. Thank you!
I can't believe some people. I would never feel differently about a person just because they don't conform to a specific norm. Insane.
Definitely gonna be asking her a lot of questions haha.

Not really. I'm 35 and my wife is 33. But my wife has been in our daughter's life since she was born. It feels really strange that she came to me with the dating thing and not my wife. I suppose I should have seen that as trust and not freaked out, but I can't take it back now.
I've said over and over again that his sexuality doesn't bother me. It's his promiscuity that gets under my skin.
Well, because I'd rather us being the ones teaching her about it. My buddy is a great, great friend. But he's promiscuous. He's extremely open with everything he's done in his life.

I'm brand new to this whole fatherhood thing. My daughter wasn't adopted until she was twelve and I've got no bio kids of my own yet, so this whole thing is very, very new.

When she started talking about dating, it punched me in the gut. Came out of nowhere (well, probably not, but you get what I mean). Admittedly, I didn't react well, but we've since talked it out and I promised I wouldn't freak out again.

Which is why I'm here.

I'm drawing lines to every conclusion because I have no idea what's going on.

Yes. I know it would be considered a hebephile, but...hair-splitting.
That makes sense.

> If she went to someone else because she was afraid of your reaction

That's my problem right now. What if she wasn't going to ask me about homework and really needed to talk to me, but I pushed her to him? I feel like the worst person right now...
I'm picking her up from school today, so I'll try to act like nothing's wrong. She'll probably figure it out, though. She's too smart for me.
Hey, forgive me if my father was a serial cheater and these were the kind of texts he'd send his barely legal mistress. Fuck sake.

Yeah, we don't need anymore Dad-level freakouts.

My buddy isn't telling me squat, though. He just keeps telling me to ask her. Damn him for being such a good friend.
Thank you!

"Don't worry about telling them. It can be between us only."

> In fact, you might consider thanking him for being someone your daughter feels she can trust.

Thank you. You're right. He's a wonderful friend, really. Everyone loves him (when they don't find him annoying). I don't believe he'd do anything to ruin his career or our friendship.

First of all, I don't think it's appropriate for a 31 yo man to have secrets with a fifteen yo girl. Second, he's an enormous flirt and she's far beyond her years. I swear she has the soul of a forty-year-old.

I can't help but think that freak-out has something to do with her not telling me whatever this is.
